title: Why supernatural theology is necessary; five hypotheses before the highest good can be taught
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: the highest beatitude belonging toward God's kingdom, plus belonging toward man as citizen belonging toward this kingdom, will be explained somewhat more solidly — when these stand as rightly established. fifth, the last judgment. fourth, the resurrection belonging toward the flesh; third, the end belonging toward this world; second, the state belonging toward the same when separated from its body; first, the immortality belonging toward the rational soul; namely: — that good cannot be taught clearly enough unless other hypotheses have already been settled in the reader's mind. namely because it raises plus directs his true practice — that same which stands as according to piety — above nature to his highest end plus to the good belonging toward eternal joy plus glory. From that same which it stands as gathered at once what plus why this supernatural doctrine plus theology stands as necessary toward man beside plus beyond the natural sciences: So Thomas.
pass_b_english: So Thomas. From which it is gathered at once what and why this supernatural doctrine and theology is necessary for man beside and beyond the natural sciences: namely because it raises and directs his true practice — which is according to piety — above nature to his highest end and to the good of eternal joy and glory.

That good cannot be taught clearly enough unless other hypotheses have already been settled in the reader's mind, namely: first, the immortality of the rational soul; second, the state of the same when separated from its body; third, the end of this world; fourth, the resurrection of the flesh; fifth, the last judgment.
When these are rightly established, the highest beatitude of God's kingdom, and of man as citizen of this kingdom, will be explained somewhat more solidly.
source_text: Haec Thomas, ex quibus simul colligitur, quod & quare homini praeter & ultra naturales scientias, haec supernaturalis doctrina & Theologia sit necessaria, quippe quae veram ipsius praxin, quae secundum pietatem est, evehit & dirigit supra naturam ad summum finem suum & bonum gaudii & gloriae aeternae. Quod bonum luculente satis doceri nequit, nisi aliae hypotheses jam ante in animo lectoris firmatae sint, nimirum, 1. Animae rationalis immortalitas. 2. Ejusdem a corpore suo separatae status. 3. Hujus mundi finis. 4. Resurrectio carnis. 5. Judicium extremum. Quibus recte constitutis, summa regni Dei, hominisque civis hujus regni, beatitudo aliquanto solidius explicabitur.
